evidence: InMemoryTaskRepository implements TaskRepository (domain port), so it is a persistence adapter.
add*/find* methods only call Map.set or Map.get on private Maps. This is pure storage.
tasksForProject filters on projectId, status and assigneeId using the caller's TaskFilter. This is query criteria, not domain policy.
There is no HTTP or request handling and no business decision logic in the file.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file is an in-memory adapter for persistence. It implements the domain TaskRepository port. Its methods only store and look up records: addUser, findUser, addProject, findProject, addTask and findTask. tasksForProject applies the caller's TaskFilter, matching on projectId, status and assigneeId. Filtering by query criteria is ordinary repository query work. It doesn't decide state transitions, permissions or invariants, so it isn't a business rule. Nothing in the file handles transport or presentation either. Every responsibility fits the infrastructure layer.
